handoff.purpose: Defines scope_key, resolution_context, cached_index, _hotspots, and score_modules with caching and locking logic.

symbols.name: scope_key
symbols.note: Builds a scope key string from resolved path, scope, and flags (documents, types, wiki).

symbols.note: Returns a SymbolResolver from _RESOLVER_CACHE based on key or repo root; references undefined _RESOLVER_CACHE.

claims.text: THE SUFFIX ORDER IS FIXED -- ``base`` then ``+docs`` then ``+types`` -- so the four flag combinations produce four distinct keys and no two of them can collide by being spelled in a different order.
claims.why: In the code, base is extended sequentially: +docs, then +types, then +wiki. The order is fixed as claimed.

claims.text: ``key`` is an index's ``scope_key``; pass it whenever you hold the index dict, so a SCOPED index gets the resolver built under that same scope rather than whichever build last touched the bare root.
claims.why: The function uses _RESOLVER_CACHE which is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify behavior.

claims.text: Omitting it keeps the historical bare-root lookup for unscoped callers.
claims.why: Same as above; depends on _RESOLVER_CACHE not present.

claims.text: Process-wide index cache keyed by resolved repo root.
claims.why: The code uses resolved = Path(repo_root).resolve() and keys _INDEX_CACHE with _scope_key(...) which includes resolved.
If refresh is True, the code pops the key from cache before checking under lock.

claims.text: SINGLE-FLIGHT (load-bearing): the cache is only populated *after* a build finishes, so without a per-root lock every concurrent caller saw a cold cache and started its OWN full scan.
claims.why: The code uses _build_lock(key) to ensure only one build per key; cache is populated after build inside the locked block.

claims.text: Concurrent callers now block on the in-flight build and share its result.
claims.why: The lock ensures one build; subsequent callers wait on lock and then find the cache populated.

claims.text: The scope fingerprint is PART OF THE KEY: the cached index is a function of the center and the ignore rules as well as the root, so changing either must not hand back the index built under the old scope.
claims.why: scope = project_scope(resolved, center, ignore) is called and used in _scope_key, so scope influences the key.

claims.text: An unscoped repo keeps its bare path key, so nothing changes for repos that never configure this.
claims.why: In scope_key, if unscoped (not center and not ignore), base is just str(resolved) without fingerprint.

claims.text: ``documents`` is resolved ONCE, here, and the same resolved boolean is used for both the key and the build.
claims.why: docs_on = documents_enabled(documents) is computed once and passed to both _scope_key and build_index.

claims.text: ``types`` is resolved here for the same reason and with the same hazard: a key built from one reading of the env var and a build from another would cache a type-bearing index under the key for a type-free one.
claims.why: types_on = types_enabled(types) is computed once and used in both key and build.

claims.text: ``wiki`` follows the identical discipline, and for the identical hazard: resolved ONCE here so the key and the build cannot disagree.
claims.why: wiki_on = wiki_enabled(wiki) and docs_on is computed once and used in both key and build.

claims.text: Base score = long fns * 3 + guard_count + loc/50 (+ cc_max if present).
claims.why: The calculation is not present in this chunk; only the formula is stated.
The calculation is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: If ``churn`` is empty/None the factor is exactly 1.0 -> behaves identically to the pre-churn ranking (no regression); a ``churn`` field is added to every row regardless.
claims.why: The implementation is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Returned whole rather than pre-trimmed so the code map can heat-shade every node from the same scoring pass that produces the hotspot list.
claims.why: The return statement is not in this chunk.

scope_key docstring mentions 'four flag combinations' but the function only has three flag parameters (documents, types, wiki). The scope itself is not a flag; the combinations are 2^3=8 possibilities, not 4. The docstring may be outdated.
cached_index docstring describes single-flight locking; the implementation uses a per-key lock and rechecks under lock, which matches the claim.
